Resolve a Bakery image layout into an unpopulated disk image.

## Inputs

| Name     | Kind      | Description                                                      |
| -------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `layout` | file      | Rugix ImageLayout definition in JSON or TOML.                    |
| `roots`  | directory | Prepared filesystem trees addressed by each partition root path. |
| `layer`  | directory | Layer tree containing roots/ and any referenced firmware blobs.  |

## Parameters

| Name   | Default | Description                                                            |
| ------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size` | `0`     | Disk capacity in bytes. Zero uses the capacity required by the layout. |

## Outputs

| Name    | Kind | Description                                                              |
| ------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `image` | file | Sparse disk image containing its partition table and raw firmware blobs. |

## Execution

| Setting      | Value   |
| ------------ | ------- |
| Environment  | Bakery  |
| Output cache | Allowed |

Resolve a Bakery `ImageLayout` into an unpopulated disk. This rule supports GPT,
MBR with extended partitions, and raw firmware written before partitions. It
preserves the layout model used by system image configuration and BSPs.

The `roots` input contains prepared filesystem trees under their root names. The
`layer` input supplies paths referenced by raw firmware blobs. For example, a
partition with `root = "system"` reads its size estimate from `roots/system`,
while a blob with `file = "bsp/firmware.bin"` reads that file from the layer
input.

A partition with an explicit size keeps that capacity. Otherwise, Bakery
estimates capacity from its tree, with a minimum of 64 MiB and 20% overhead. The
output contains partition tables and raw firmware, with empty partition regions.
Disk and partition identifiers derive from the layout and resolved geometry. Raw
firmware reservations must not overlap, exceed their reserved capacity, or
overwrite partition table metadata.

For example, this Bakery `ImageLayout` describes one ext4 root partition:

```toml title="layouts/device.toml"
type = "gpt"

[[partitions]]
root = "system"
filesystem = { type = "ext4" }
```

The layout records the intended filesystem; this rule resolves geometry without
creating that filesystem. An invocation binds the layout and its prepared trees:

```toml
uses = "core/image-layout"
inputs.layout = { file = "layouts/device.toml" }
inputs.roots = { file = "prepared-roots" }
inputs.layer = { file = "prepared-layer" }
```

Use `core/assemble-disk` to populate the partitions with separately built
filesystem artifacts.
